summary: Highland (Red) Lookout on Red Mountain south of Butte: a site developed about 1933, a present L-4 cab built in 1954, now listed as available for emergencies.

access.note: Listed as available for emergencies; no public rental or visitor program found. Reached by an unpaved, seasonal summit road.

visit.trail_note: Fish Creek Road is unpaved, needs a high-clearance 4x4, and is usually impassable October to June. With no snow and enough clearance, a four-wheel-drive trail runs to a gate just over 9,000 ft.

events.note: First L-4 structure on the site. firelookout.com says an L-4 cab on the summit; NHLR calls it an L-4 groundhouse.
Present L-4 cab on a concrete base replaced the 1933 structure. firelookout.com places it about 1/4 mile north of Red Mtn.
Lightning strike on August 22, 1922, on a group of Butte Boy Scouts during a hike. One scout died and others were injured.
Registered as NHLR US 927 (MT 55) on September 24, 2011.
Memorial monument installed beside the tower to the 1922 lightning strike.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources disagree on what came before the 1954 cab. NHLR says it replaced an L-4 groundhouse built in 1933. firelookout.com says the site was developed about 1933 with an L-4 cab on the summit. The story reports both.

dangerousroads.org places the 1954 tower at the summit. firelookout.com puts the present cab about 1/4 mile north of Red Mtn. SummitPost says it is below the peak. The story follows firelookout.com for the distance and says the sources differ.
NHLR gives 9,701 ft (2,957 m), which matches the brief. firelookout.com lists 10,070 ft and 9,701 ft without saying which is the tower. The record keeps 9,701 ft.

notes_for_editor: No fire at this site appears in the sources read. The brief's kind two_story is not verified: NHLR describes an L-4 cab on a one-story concrete base, and a search snippet quoting a firelookout.org directory (not read) called it a two-story cab. Left unchanged. Consider whether the 1954 event should be replaced rather than built. Staffing and current access are unconfirmed; no Forest Service page was read. One WebSearch was used.
